title: Marie Curie's Life In Reverse, From the Pantheon to Warsaw #Shorts
description:
Marie Curie's life runs backwards in this episode, from her death in a French mountain sanatorium in 1934 back to her birth in a Warsaw classroom in 1867. The journey steps through her two Nobel Prizes, the tonnes of pitchblende residue boiled down in a leaking shed, the X-ray cars she drove toward the front in the First World War, and the freezing room in the Latin Quarter where she first counted her own francs. Every scene moves to an earlier year, so the discoveries arrive in reverse order and the costs behind them become visible. Dates, places and measurements follow the documented record of her life.

Made with AI assistance.

scenes.narration: This is the end of a life that began in a Warsaw classroom. Marie Curie died in 1934, and a year later her daughter took a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
Step backwards and she is driving an X-ray car toward the trenches of the First World War, teaching women to find a bullet in the dark.
Further back she boils tonnes of ore in a leaking shed and isolates radium, then wins a second Nobel Prize, this time on her own.
Before that she marries Pierre Curie, earns two degrees at the Sorbonne, and counts every franc in a freezing room in the Latin Quarter.
At the start there is a girl in Poland with no university that will admit her, raised by a teacher father who kept glass instruments at home.
